turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I'm Meredith Kalinowski, Owen's mother. I have until 4:40, so tell me why my son has a zero.
Thanks for coming in, Ms. Kalinowski.
Okay. You asked for this meeting, Hale, so go ahead. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen spoken to before it went in?
The school's AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94 percent.
A machine's guess. Even the company that sells it says not to use it alone, and I have that printed in my bag. So what else do you have, Hale?
That's very high. The software is quite reliable.
"Quite reliable." Your own school's procedure, 4.3, says software results don't by themselves establish a concern. I'll ask once more, Hale: what else do you have, other than a number?
So I had to give him a zero.

"Had to." So you decided first and asked questions later, and procedure 4.2 says you call a parent before any mark goes in. Nobody called me, Hale. Owen found out on his phone, in the middle of class.
I hope you understand my position.
"Your position" is a zero with no document behind it. Take it off the gradebook, Hale, and then we can talk about what comes next.
